papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is standard of care for inoperable stage I or II non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). KEYNOTE-867 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03924869) evaluated the addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT in participants diagnosed with stage I or II NSCLC that was inoperable or in participants who refused surgery. METHODS: Adults with untreated, stage I or II (T1 to limited T3, N0, M0) NSCLC (AJCC 8th edition) that was inoperable, or adults who refused surgery, were randomly assigned 1:1 to thoracic SBRT to primary tumors for ≤2 weeks concomitantly with pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo once every 3 weeks for ≤17 cycles. The primary end point was event-free survival (EFS) by blinded independent central review. RESULTS: A total of 448 participants were randomly assigned to SBRT plus pembrolizumab (n = 227) or SBRT plus placebo (n = 221). The median time from random assignment to the data cutoff date (June 11, 2024) for the prespecified first interim analysis was 20.6 (range, 1.3-56.8) months. The median EFS (95% CI) was 31.2 (22.5 to 39.1) months and 28.3 (19.8 to 33.1) months for the pembrolizumab and placebo arms, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.69 to 1.24]; P = .2932). Among participants who received ≥1 dose of study treatment, grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 46/226 (20.4%) participants in the pembrolizumab arm and 8/218 (3.7%) participants in the placebo arm. There were five treatment-related deaths all of which occurred in the pembrolizumab arm (2.2%). CONCLUSION: The addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT did not improve EFS and was associated with a higher incidence of treatment-related AEs compared with SBRT alone in participants with inoperable stage I or II NSCLC. Based on the benefit-risk profile, the KEYNOTE-867 trial was prematurely stopped, and all study treatment was discontinued.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria. RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods. CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Physical deterioration and disease progression during neoadjuvant treatment can preclude tumor surgery in patients with gastroesophageal cancer. Whether preoperative exercise training can increase the probability of undergoing tumor surgery remains unknown. OBJECTIVE: To compare exercise training with usual care on the likelihood of not undergoing tumor surgery with curative intent after neoadjuvant treatment for gastroesophageal cancer. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: PRESET-RCT was a single-blinded, parallel-group, 2-arm, superiority randomized clinical trial. Patients with gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma scheduled to undergo treatment with curative intent, including neoadjuvant treatment, and with no contraindication to exercise training were eligible. Participants were enrolled at University Hospital Copenhagen, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark, from August 16, 2018, to September 23, 2022, with final follow-up on October 22, 2024. Data analysis was performed from March 2023 to May 2025. INTERVENTION: The participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative exercise training from diagnosis until tumor surgery or control. The intervention consisted of twice-weekly concurrent aerobic exercise and resistance training. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was not undergoing tumor surgery with curative intent. The secondary outcomes were treatment tolerance and overall survival. RESULTS: In total, 207 participants (73.7%) were randomized and 202 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analyses (mean [SD] age, 65.3 [8.5] years; 161 [78.9%] male; 170 [83.3%] with gastroesophageal junction cancer), with 101 randomized to each group. In the exercise group, 10 (9.9%) did not undergo tumor surgery with curative intent compared with 8 (7.9%) in the control group (odds ratio, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.48-3.38; P = .62). There were no between-group differences in permanent discontinuation of neoadjuvant treatment (odds ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.38-1.72) or postoperative complications (odds ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.61-2.20). The overall survival rates at 3 years for the exercise and control group were 51.0% and 65.0%, respectively (hazard ratio, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.02-2.45). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, preoperative exercise training did not increase the likelihood of undergoing tumor surgery for patients with gastroesophageal cancer. The findings do not support the use of exercise training during neoadjuvant treatment to improve surgical outcomes, and further research is needed to determine its effects on long-term outcomes. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03490565.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: In clinical trials, the messenger RNA (mRNA)-1345 vaccine provided protection against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) illness. Data on mRNA-1345 effectiveness in broader patient populations are needed. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effectiveness of mRNA-1345 vaccination during a single respiratory illness season. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used a target trial emulation framework to assess veterans 50 years and older receiving care in the Veterans Health Administration. Eligible vaccine recipients were matched with up to 4 unvaccinated individuals in 4 monthly, nested, sequential trials from October 1, 2025, to January 31, 2026. Outcomes were ascertained through May 31, 2026, or 24 weeks. EXPOSURE: A single dose of mRNA-1345 RSV vaccine vs no RSV vaccination. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was any positive RSV test result from day 14 after the matched index date. Secondary outcomes included RSV-associated emergency department (ED) or urgent care (UC) encounters and RSV-associated hospitalizations. Vaccine effectiveness was estimated as 100 × (1 - risk ratio). A sensitivity analysis comparing veterans who received same-day mRNA-1345 and influenza vaccination to influenza vaccination alone (active comparator arm) was performed to explore potential bias from differences in health care-seeking behavior and outcome ascertainment between comparator groups. RESULTS: A total of 74 926 vaccinated veterans were matched to 286 425 unique control individuals, weighted to represent 74 926 individuals, for a total of 149 852 study participants (median [IQR] age, 73.0 [63.3-78.6] years; 136 756 [91.3%] male). During a median (IQR) follow-up of 160 (130-168) days, estimated vaccine effectiveness was 60.3% (95% CI, 49.0%-70.4%) against any documented infection, 60.2% (95% CI, 47.2%-71.5%) against RSV-associated ED or UC encounters, and 81.8% (95% CI, 58.1%-99.9%) against RSV-associated hospitalizations. Estimated effectiveness against documented infections decreased with increasing age, from 82.9% (95% CI, 64.0%-96.7%) in the 50- to 59-year age group to 28.6% (95% CI, -12.0% to 60.4%) in the 80-year or older age group. With an active comparator arm, estimated effectiveness was 67.1% (95% CI, 48.9%-82.6%) against documented RSV infections, 69.5% (95% CI, 49.7%-85.4%) against RSV-associated ED and UC encounters, and 86.9% (95% CI, 56.5%-100.0%) against RSV-associated hospitalizations. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study using a target trial emulation of mRNA-1345 vaccine effectiveness during 24 weeks, vaccination was associated with protection against RSV illness and associated health care use in adults 50 years and older. Comparative effectiveness studies are needed to determine the relative benefits of available RSV vaccine products.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Recurrent pulmonary exacerbations contribute substantially to lung function decline in people with cystic fibrosis (CF). Inhalation therapies are a cornerstone of standard of care, yet adherence to inhalation therapies is variable and data on the relationship between adherence and pulmonary exacerbations remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To assess the impact of multimodal telemonitoring and coaching on adherence and pulmonary exacerbations in people with CF. METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter, unblinded, randomized, controlled trial people with CF aged ≥12 years were randomized (1:1) to either standard of care or an intervention involving continuous objective home monitoring of inhalation adherence, weekly home spirometry, a self-management app, professional telephone coaching, and optional video conferencing over 18 months. The primary endpoint was time to first pulmonary exacerbation. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: 296 participants were included with a mean age of 31.3 (SD 10.8) years, 54.1% females, mean FEV1% predicted of 70.2% (SD 24.7), 52.7% chronically infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and 85.1% on triple CFTR modulator therapy. Baseline adherence was higher in the intervention group (58.1%) than in the control group (44.0%) and remained higher throughout the study (last 6 months: 49.2% vs. 32.6%). Time to first exacerbation did not differ between groups. However, across all participants, a 10% increase in adherence correlated with a 9% reduction in pulmonary exacerbation risk. Participants with FEV1<40% had a 2.4-fold higher risk of exacerbations. CONCLUSION: Multimodal telemedicine improved inhalation therapy adherence. The association between higher adherence and reduced exacerbations highlights the ongoing importance of inhalation therapy in CF, even with widespread CFTR modulator use. Clinical trial registered with German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00024642).

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Sepsis-associated lung injury (SALI) is a lethal infection-induced complication with high mortality and limited targeted therapies. Dysregulated lactate metabolism is closely linked to SALI, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the role and molecular mechanism of EZH2 (Enhancer of zeste homolog 2) lactylation in SALI development, thereby uncovering a novel exploitable therapeutic target. METHODS: A total of 209 ICU patients were enrolled and divided into the SALI group (n = 104) and non-SALI group (n = 105) to detect serum lactate levels. papers.abstract_en: Esophageal cancer (EC) is highly lethal due to late diagnosis, and accurate non-invasive tools for early detection and subtyping remain lacking. Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) fragmentomics offers a promising biomarker source. The PSP model distinguished ESCC from EAC with 89.71% accuracy, improving to 90.74% after integrating key clinical parameters. papers.abstract_en: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has improved clinical outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve durable responses, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory inhibitor subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a metabolic driver of immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC through RNA sequencing of tumors with differential responses to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy. PPP1R1B was significantly upregulated in non-responders and correlated with poor prognosis in NSCLC patients. Mechanistically, PPP1R1B directly interacted with IRF3 through the Arg29 residue and promoted dephosphorylation of IRF3 at Ser396, thereby suppressing IRF3 activation and downstream interferon-β (IFN-β) signaling. Blockade of IFN-β signaling abrogated the antitumor effects induced by PPP1R1B depletion, supporting an immune-dependent mechanism. Notably, tumors resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy exhibited impaired oxidative phosphorylation and excessive lactate accumulation. Lactate induced PPP1R1B expression through NF-κB-dependent transcriptional activation, linking metabolic reprogramming to innate immune suppression. Collectively, our findings identify a lactate/NF-κB/PPP1R1B/IRF3 signaling axis that drives immune evasion and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in NSCLC, and nominate PPP1R1B as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterize pleuroparenchymal abnormalities identified on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) in cancer patients investigated for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE) and to compare imaging findings between patients with and without confirmed PE. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 113 consecutive cancer patients who underwent CTPA for suspected acute PE between January 2022 and January 2026. Imaging findings were compared between PE-positive and PE-negative groups. An exploratory multivariable model with a restricted set of imaging predictors was constructed to limit overfitting, with correction for multiple comparisons and bootstrap-based internal validation. Exploratory subgroup analyses by malignancy type and disease burden were also performed. RESULTS: PE was confirmed in 32 patients (28.3%). The median age was 59 years (IQR, 51-65), and 42.5% were female. The highest PE prevalence was observed in gastrointestinal, gynecologic, and thoracic malignancies. At nominal testing, infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity was more frequent in PE-positive patients (12.5% vs. 1.2%; OR, 11.43; p = 0.022), whereas ground-glass opacity (15.6% vs. 35.8%; OR, 0.33; p = 0.041) and interstitial/septal change (3.1% vs. 25.9%; OR, 0.09; p = 0.007) were less frequent. None remained statistically significant after false-discovery-rate correction (q = 0.133, 0.166, and 0.082, respectively). The parsimonious model had an apparent AUROC of 0.707 and an optimism-adjusted AUROC of 0.699, with acceptable grouped calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.522). No exploratory cancer-subgroup comparison met q < 0.05. CONCLUSIONS: Pleuroparenchymal abnormalities are highly prevalent in cancer patients undergoing CTPA for suspected PE; however, most findings are nonspecific. Infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity generated the strongest exploratory PE-associated signal, but no individual imaging comparison survived multiplicity correction and model estimates remained imprecise. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: T-cell function is regulated by immunometabolism, and lysosomes are signaling hubs. CD68 (LAMP4), traditionally regarded as a monocyte/macrophage marker, has been largely neglected in T cell biology. We aimed to assess the link between CD68 expression in T cells and anti-PD-1 response in lung cancer, and its potential as an early dynamic biomarker in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells. METHODS: We analyzed transcriptomic (GSE126044, GSE135222, GSE166449) and single-cell (GSE207422) data from anti-PD-1-treated lung cancer cohorts to identify lysosome related pathways and key genes, validated with peripheral blood CD8+ T cell data (GSE111414). Prospectively, we enrolled lung cancer patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, collecting peripheral blood at baseline and week 3. Flow cytometry measured CD68 in CD8+ T cells and subsets, assessing association with response, progression-free survival (PFS), and functional markers (granzyme B, perforin, Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, IL-1β). RESULTS: Responders showed enrichment of lysosome pathways and upregulation of 8 lysosome related genes including CD68, positively correlated with monocyte and T cell infiltration. Single-cell data linked CD68 expression in T cell to favorable response. After one cycle, the proportion of CD8+CD68+ T cells was lower in non-responders (P<0.05), with AUC 0.803 (P=0.044) and cutoff 1.015%, stratifying PFS (P=0.0225). CD68 was highest in naïve T cells at baseline, but decreased across subsets after treatment in non-responders (all P<0.01). Functionally, compared with CD8+CD68- T cells, CD8+CD68+ T cells exhibited lower expression of granzyme B and perforin but higher expression of Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, and IL-1β (all P<0.001), suggesting a CD8+ T cell state characterized by lower cytotoxicity and enhanced proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, accompanied by a tissue residency associated phenotype. CONCLUSION: CD8+CD68+ T cells exhibit lower cytotoxicity but greater proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, together with a tissue residency associated phenotype, suggesting a precursor-like state. Low CD68 expression in tumor-infiltrating T cells and the post-treatment reduction of CD68 expression in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells are associated with resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer. These findings suggest that CD8+CD68+ T cells may serve as a potential early dynamic immune biomarker for monitoring and assessing response to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sequencing respiratory virus genomes is essential for public health surveillance and research. Although shotgun metagenomics is pathogen agnostic, its sensitivity is limited by abundant off-target host nucleic acids. Hybridization bait capture overcomes this limitation by selectively enriching viral sequences prior to sequencing. METHODS: We evaluated three respiratory viral bait capture workflows (veSEQ, RVI-seq, and Illumina) to compare their performance and assess their suitability for scalable respiratory virus sequencing. Synthetic RNA controls and clinical samples containing SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, human parainfluenza virus, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were analysed. RESULTS: All three workflows demonstrated high efficiency, reproducibility and broadly comparable performance across respiratory viruses. Complete viral genomes were consistently recovered from samples containing 10,000 viral copies, while viral reads remained detectable at substantially lower viral loads, including approximately 100 copies. Workflow optimisation reduced reagent costs and enabled laboratory automation without compromising sequencing sensitivity. CONCLUSION: Hybridization bait capture provides an effective and scalable approach for respiratory virus genome sequencing. Cost reductions and automation can be implemented without compromising performance, supporting its use in routine genomic surveillance and public health preparedness.

papers.abstract_en: The tumor microenvironment is a critical factor in understanding cancer progression and metastasis. In this context, isolating tumor interstitial fluid (TIF) is a powerful tool for detecting cancer biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In our study, we conducted a proteomic analysis of TIFs from metastatic lung nodules using a murine model. The TIFs from these lungs were enriched with actin-binding proteins, among other molecules. Notably, we identified Scinderin (Scin), an actin-binding protein secreted by tumor cells. Knockdown of Scin resulted in a significant decrease in the number and size of lung nodules, as well as a reduction, albeit to a lesser extent, in disseminated tumor cells (DTCs). Furthermore, silencing Scin inhibited cell and tumor growth in different cancer cell lines. In human tumors, Scin was detected in the tumor interstitial fluid (TIF) of endometrial cancer patients. Scin was expressed abundantly in serous endometrial carcinomas and in the secretory endometrium. Remarkably, a paired analysis using an endometrial cancer tissue-array revealed increased Scin expression in metastatic samples compared to their corresponding primary tumors. In addition, a retrospective study revealed that levels of Scin in plasma were significantly elevated in patients who developed metastases. These findings suggest that Scin plays a significant role in the metastatic process and may serve as a promising biomarker for tumor aggressiveness and metastatic potential.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The cultures of human nasal epithelial cells (NECs) are good surrogate models for studying immune responses. Three-dimensional (3D) organoids have emerged as an alternative for nasal epithelium, serving as robust platforms for modeling respiratory viral infections. We aimed to generate human NEC organoids and to determine their cellular characteristics as an in vitro model for air-liquid interface (ALI) culture and influenza A virus (IAV) infection. METHODS: Primary human nasal mucosal tissues were obtained from healthy donors undergoing nasal surgery, and nasal epithelial cell (NEC) organoids were established using Matrigel-based three-dimensional culture. Differentiated NEC organoids and air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures were characterized by histology, immunostaining, electron microscopy, and quantitative real-time PCR, followed by influenza A virus (A/WS/33, H1N1) infection assays. In addition, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to analyze cellular heterogeneity and differentiation trajectories of NEC organoids. RESULTS: We successfully developed human NEC organoids with using a Matrigel-based 3D culture system that recapitulates the structural characteristics and cellular composition of the human nasal epithelium. Histological results, real-time PCR, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) revealed that the organoids consisted of seven different cell types and displayed a difference in the composition between the cells. The organoids displayed a much higher rate of basal progenitor cells whereas ciliated cells were less dominant. Unlike ALI cultures in which passage (P) 2 was the limit, the organoids exhibited successful and subsequent passages up to P5. Our data determined that NEC organoids are an adequate in vitro model for IAV infection and showed a sharp induction of mRNA levels for interferons (IFNs) and IFN-stimulated genes following IAV infection. CONCLUSIONS: This study's results demonstrate that human NEC organoids serve as a robust in vitro model, successfully recapitulating the biological characteristics of nasal epithelium, and could be an adequate tool for exploring distinct IFN-related innate immune responses following influenza infection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic inflammatory airway disease, characterised by dysregulated interactions between innate and adaptive immune cells. Although Th2-mediated inflammation predominates, persistent Th17-associated immune responses contribute to chronic airway inflammation implicated in the corticosteroid-insensitive disease state. Fluoxetine, a SSRI with immunomodulatory properties, was investigated to determine its effects on inflammation and Th17 response in experimental allergic airway disease. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Immunomodulatory effects of fluoxetine evaluated in exploratory in vitro assays. In vivo studies were performed in an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model of allergic asthma using oral fluoxetine at clinically relevant doses. Airway pathology, immunophenotypes, cytokine production, gene and protein expression were evaluated by histology, flow cytometry, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), confocal microscopy and ex vivo functional assays. Public transcriptomic datasets were integrated with target enrichment analyses, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations used to explore potential molecular interactions. KEY RESULTS: Fluoxetine reduced the inflammatory response in activated macrophages without noticeable cytotoxicity. In an allergic asthma model, fluoxetine attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, eosinophilia, IgE production and pulmonary macrophage activation, whilst reducing the accumulation of the phenotypically granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor like cell population along with diminished T-cell activation and reduced Th17 responses, reduced IL-17 production together with decreased expression and nuclear localisation of RORγt. Ex vivo studies confirmed inhibition of RORγt expression and IL-17 production in Th17 cells. Transcriptomic integration identified significant enrichment of Th17-associated inflammatory pathways, whereas molecular docking and molecular dynamics analyses supported RORγt as a plausible molecular target. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Fluoxetine attenuates experimental allergic airway inflammation through coordinated modulation of innate and adaptive immune responses, with suppression of the RORγt-IL-17 signalling axis emerging as a key mechanistic feature. These findings expand the immunopharmacological profile of fluoxetine and provide an experimental rationale for further investigating its therapeutic potential in Th17-associated airway inflammatory diseases and in experimental models that more closely recapitulate corticosteroid-resistant asthma.

papers.abstract_en: The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is a conserved and compelling target for pan-coronavirus antiviral development. To date, all US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved RdRp inhibitors are nucleotide inhibitors (NIs), which are prone to drug resistance and show limited clinical efficacy. Developing alternative non-nucleotide inhibitors (NNIs) with high target specificity, structural diversity, and metabolic stability could yield more effective antivirals. Here, we identify an allosteric RdRp NNI, BAY-850, via computational screening. BAY-850 exhibits potent, broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants and other human coronaviruses. Mechanistic studies show that BAY-850 binds directly to a previously unrecognized allosteric site on nsp12, thereby fine-tuning the catalytic motif F loop out-conformation the orthosteric site. Importantly, therapeutic administration of BAY-850 significantly reduces viral loads in the nasal turbinates and lungs of SARS-CoV-2-infected K18-hACE2 mice. These findings validate a novel allosteric site in RdRp and support BAY-850 as a start-point for broad-spectrum anti-coronavirus development.

papers.abstract_en: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 has led to a global pandemic, causing unprecedented disruption to health systems and economies worldwide, calling for an urgent imperative for precise and sensitive diagnostic method. To address this, a novel detection method, termed antibody‒nucleic acid conjugate linked immunosorbent assay (ANCLISA), was designed for the ultra-sensitive detection of the receptor binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2, which play a pivotal role in the diagnosis of COVID-19. Leveraging the Alphafold 2 model for simulating antibody‒antigen complexes and the ΔΔG predictor model for forecasting the binding free energy of antigen‒antibody complex, we successfully identified the high-affinity antibody TB1. Through the utilization of succinimidyl 4-[N-maleimidomethyl] cyclohexane-1-carboxylate (SMCC) for antibody‒nucleic acid conjugation and the integration of the hybridization chain reaction (HCR) for signal amplification within the system, we have established an ultra-sensitive approach for the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant detection. The proposed immunoassay provided exhibited a linear detection range spanning 11 fg/mL to 11 ng/mL, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.48 fg/mL. Our innovative approach represents a significant stride in enabling precise and ultra-sensitive detection of SARS-CoV-2, thereby holding promise for enhancing diagnostic capabilities in the ongoing global battle against the pandemic.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Human adenovirus type 7(HAdV-7) is a major cause of severe pediatric pneumonia, but the mechanisms linking viral infection to pulmonary immune remodeling and lung pathology remain incompletely understood. Progress has been limited by the lack of physiologically relevant animal models that recapitulate human susceptibility. METHODS: We generated human CD46 (hCD46) humanized mice and evaluated pulmonary viral burden, recoverable infectious virus, and lung pathology after HAdV-7 infection. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on lung tissues from wild type and hCD46 humanized mice under control and infected conditions to characterize cellular composition, transcriptional states, and intercellular communication. Human PBMC bulk transcriptomes from pediatric HAdV infection were further analyzed to assess the systemic relevance of mouse lung derived immune programs. RESULTS: hCD46 humanized mice showed increased pulmonary viral burden, recoverable infectious virions, and more severe lung pathology after HAdV-7 infection. Single-cell profiling revealed depletion of resident alveolar macrophages, pronounced expansion of inflammatory macrophage subsets, and remodeling of lymphoid transcriptional states in infected hCD46 lungs. These changes were accompanied by prominent type I/II interferon and interferon associated chemokine programs. B cells and CD4+ and CD8+ T cells showed prominent interferon stimulated genes (ISGs) associated transcriptional states, together with alterations in selected effector- and memory-associated programs and computationally inferred trajectories. Projection of mouse lung derived signatures onto transcriptomes of human peripheral blood mononuclear cell showed that selected interferon associated myeloid and lymphoid programs were also detectable systemically in pediatric HAdV infection. CONCLUSIONS: HAdV-7 infection in hCD46 humanized mice was associated with an interferon enriched pulmonary inflammatory environment, prominent inflammatory myeloid remodeling, and altered lymphoid transcriptional states. This susceptible mouse model provides a useful experimental tool for studying HAdV-7 associated lung disease and for preclinical evaluation of antiviral, immunomodulatory, and vaccine strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS) is a severe respiratory condition characterized by acute, diffuse inflammatory damage to the lungs, posing a significant threat to human health. Although neutrophils and macrophages are known to play critical roles in ALI/ARDS pathogenesis, the precise cellular pathways governing their interaction remain poorly defined, and targeted therapeutics modulating these pathways are currently lacking. Here, we show that macrophages secrete CCL5 to activate CCR1 on neutrophils, thereby driving neutrophil chemotaxis toward the lungs in ALI. Mechanistically, this signaling axis operates primarily through Giα2-dependent suppression of intracellular cAMP levels. Pharmacological inhibition of CCR1 with BX471 blocks this pathway and attenuates ALI progression. Furthermore, we developed a nanoparticle-based delivery system encapsulating BX471 that exploits the intrinsic bone marrow-homing property of CXCR4high senescent neutrophils. This neutrophil‑guided strategy enables targeted drug release within the bone marrow, effectively inhibiting neutrophil egress to the lungs at the source. This approach not only significantly alleviates ALI by reducing drug dosage and administration frequency but also offers the superior safety advantage of being non-toxic to cells and tissues. Together, our findings reveal a key cellular communication axis in ALI/ARDS and present a novel, cell‑guided therapeutic strategy for targeted intervention in inflammatory lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Asthma is a heterogeneous disease with well-documented sex differences in prevalence. However, the sex-specific and pubertal effects of inhaled corticosteroids on endogenous steroid metabolites and their relationship with asthma-related clinical outcomes remain poorly understood. METHODS: Targeted serum profiling of the steroid biosynthesis pathway was generated by Precion Inc. (NC, USA). Sixteen metabolites from the steroid biosynthesis pathway were quantified at baseline and end-of-trial in children with asthma from the Childhood Asthma Management Program (CAMP; n = 1,041; metabolomics analytic subset n = 664), aged 5-12 years. Linear mixed models and generalized linear models were used to evaluate sex-specific longitudinal and endpoint responses of steroid metabolites and clinical outcomes with inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) use, adjusting for age, sex, race, height, and body mass index. RESULTS: ICS use in males was associated with significantly lower cortisol and cortisone levels at Year 4 (end of trial). In females, cortisol and cortisone showed more stable trajectories with ICS use, which resulted in a non-significant reduction at year 4. Males receiving ICS showed suggestive positive longitudinal associations for 17α-hydroxyprogesterone, estrone, and testosterone, while females showed a suggestive positive trajectory for androstenedione. ICS exposure modified the associations between metabolites and clinical outcomes (FEV1, FVC, eosinophils, and airway hyperresponsiveness) in a pathway- and sex-specific manner. Overall, ICS attenuated longitudinal associations between endogenous steroids and clinical outcomes, particularly in females, while selected relationships from the androgen-lung function associations were preserved at the end of the trial. CONCLUSION: We identify sex-specific differences in ICS-associated metabolite profiles and clinical outcomes, supporting the need for further investigation into sex-informed approaches to corticosteroid use in pediatric asthma.
